citation.authors: Alcalde RE, Jinno T, Orsini MG, Sasaki A, Sugiyama RM, Matsumura T
citation.title: Soft tissue cephalometric norms in Japanese adults
citation.journal: American Journal of Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 4 differences). Every mean and SD re-read from the page image of Table II (p. 87, PDF p. 4): agree. Decisions: (1) lower lip to E-line #72: a −0.13 (as printed), b +0.13 → +0.13: the paper's whites' value is +2.00 (Ricketts' 2 mm behind) and the text says the Japanese lower lip is more prominent to the E-plane (p. 85) and the lips anteriorly positioned in all analyses (p. 88), so the printed sign is + behind; converted to the catalogue's + ahead (merge notes asked to confirm against a and the text). (2) 'Upper lip thickness' 15.11: a #77 (basic), b #78 (vermilion) → #78: Holdaway's 'upper lip thickness' is measured at the vermilion border, distinct from his 'basic upper lip thickness'; AlBarakati 2012 Table 3 restates this value as the Japanese 'UL-vermilion'. (3) #89 upper lip length: a 'same', b 'close' → close: the text calls it 'Sn-UL St' (the upper lip's stomion), lips in repose. Not a/b differences but settled here: #79 upper lip strain entered as printed (merge notes) but 'different' (never used) - the paper's strain is positive (Holdaway: basic minus vermilion thickness) while the catalogue computes #78 − #77; raised with the owner. Supernormal group (Tables III-IV, n 19) not entered (P19). Selection class-I (Class I occlusion, minor or no crowding, good facial symmetry, p. 84; no profile criterion for this group). Scale not-stated. Owner LIP-2 (8 Oct): #79 different -> same after the catalogue was flipped to Holdaway's direction. Owner LIP-4 (12 Oct, final review I-3): 'Upper lip thickness' 15.11 moved from #78 to #77 (basic thickness), close; decision (2) above is superseded.

caveats: Sample: the Japanese normal group, 211 adults (92 men, 119 women), 20-28 y, with Japanese grandparents; Class I occlusion with minor or no crowding, good facial symmetry, no orthodontic treatment or surgery; Okayama University students (p. 84). The same research group's 1998 hard-tissue sample (217) is a separate set (alcalde1998).
Sexes pooled: the paper did not split its soft-tissue norms by sex (p. 88).

Radiographs in natural head position, teeth in maximum intercuspation, lips in repose (Shimavision 1100); hand traced and digitised (Quick Ceph) (p. 84). The paper does not say whether its FH-referenced angles use FH or a true horizontal. Film magnification not stated.

Not entered: the 'supernormal' group, 19 profiles of the same 211 chosen by 10 lay judges as esthetically pleasant (Tables III-IV, pp. 87-88) - a norm describes the normal group (P19). Table IV's 'Japanese' column is quoted from Alcalde 1998, not measured here.
Table II also prints the range, minimum and maximum for each row: observed extremes, not a norm range; not entered.
Lower lip to E-line: printed −0.13 with the paper's + = behind the E-plane (whites 2.00); stored as +0.13 under the catalogue's + = ahead.

Upper lip strain (#79): printed 2.57 ± 2.73; used (same) since the catalogue's #79 was flipped to Holdaway's direction, #77 minus #78, on 8 Oct (owner LIP-2). Before that it was kept but not used (opposite sign).
Not in the catalogue: Epker's G-Sn:Sn-Me, Sn-St:St-Me and Sn-Llv:Llv-Me ratios, interlabial distance Ulv-Llv, and subnasale perpendicular to the upper lip, lower lip and chin (Table II).

Stored as +0.13 for the catalogue's + when ahead (merge notes). Printed range −5.20 to 4.30.

entries.definitionNote: The paper labels the row only 'Upper lip thickness' (Holdaway analysis) and gives no landmarks. Read as Holdaway's basic upper lip thickness (#77) by owner ruling LIP-4 (12 Oct); AlBarakati & Bindayel 2012 (Table 3, p. 30) label the same value as the thickness at the vermilion (#78), so close, not same.
entries.note: Paper row 'Upper lip thickness' (Holdaway analysis), entered as #77 by owner ruling LIP-4 (12 Oct; final review I-3); it was #78 until then. Reason: the paper's own Whites column prints 15.0 for this row and 1.5 for upper lip strain; Holdaway's strain is basic thickness minus vermilion thickness and his vermilion standard is about 13.5 mm, and 15.0 − 13.5 = 1.5, so this row is the basic thickness. Lew 1992's row with the same label (via Moate 2002) is #77 too. One value only, entered once.
